name: ZaikaNow
tagline: Food delivery in 30 cities, where match night is the busiest night of the year
summary: ZaikaNow connects 80,000 restaurants and 1.5 lakh riders with hungry customers: search, menus, cart, payments, orders, the restaurant tablet app, rider dispatch, ETAs and notifications. On IPL final night orders peak at the innings break. Riders not assigned, restaurants not seeing orders and sold-out dishes that can still be ordered keep coming back.

tour.headline: Riders are assigned in one city-wide batch every 60 seconds, so every big match night leaves thousands of orders waiting; fixing it costs 20 hours.

incidents.title: Orders waited 30 minutes for riders on Saturday night
incidents.desc: At 21:00 thousands of orders sat unassigned for up to 30 minutes while riders waited idle nearby.
whys: Orders sat unassigned for up to 30 minutes
The city-wide assignment batch took longer than its 60-second interval
Rider assignment runs as one city-wide batch every 60 seconds
incidents.lesson: A shorter interval made the overlap worse.

incidents.title: Customers ordered dishes the restaurant had marked sold out
incidents.desc: Biryani marked sold out at 20:10 could still be ordered until 21:05; 600 orders were cancelled by restaurants.
whys: Sold-out dishes could still be ordered
The app showed availability from an hour-old cache
Menu availability is cached without invalidation when restaurants change it
incidents.fix: Cut the cache time to 15 minutes.
incidents.lesson: Fifteen minutes is still a lot of cancelled biryani.

incidents.title: Restaurants stopped receiving new orders on their tablets
incidents.desc: From 20:30 to 20:55 restaurant tablets in two cities showed no new orders; customers were charged and waited.
whys: Tablets showed no new orders for 25 minutes
The long-poll connection dropped and never reconnected
The partner tablet keeps one long-poll connection with no reconnect
incidents.fix: Asked restaurants to restart their tablets.
incidents.lesson: Restaurants should not have to restart anything.

incidents.title: IPL50 coupon rejected for first-time users
incidents.desc: The IPL50 coupon was rejected as 'not eligible' for new users for the first two hours of the campaign.
whys: Eligible users could not apply the coupon
The eligibility rule was coded for the previous campaign
Coupon rules are hard-coded for each campaign

incidents.title: Search listed restaurants that had closed for the night
incidents.desc: Customers kept finding restaurants that had closed at 22:00 and their orders were rejected.
whys: Closed restaurants appeared in search
Search read restaurant status from the stale menu cache
Menu availability is cached without invalidation when restaurants change it
incidents.fix: Filtered by opening hours as well.
incidents.lesson: Restaurants close early when they run out of food.

incidents.title: Customers charged twice after tapping Pay again
incidents.desc: When payment confirmation was slow, customers tapped Pay again and 420 orders were charged twice.
whys: Some customers were charged twice
A second tap created a second payment for the same order
Payments are created without an idempotency key per order
incidents.lesson: People tap again when nothing happens.

incidents.title: App order tracking down during the India-Pakistan match
incidents.desc: Order tracking returned errors for 20 minutes at the innings break as every open app polled for status.
whys: Order tracking returned errors for 20 minutes
Every open app polled order status every 2 seconds
Apps poll order status every 2 seconds with no backoff
incidents.fix: Added servers to the tracking API.
incidents.lesson: Polling traffic grows with every open app, not every order.

incidents.title: ETA showed 15 minutes; orders took 50
incidents.desc: On Friday night ETAs promised 15 minutes while orders took 45 to 55 minutes; support chats tripled.
whys: ETAs were far too optimistic
ETA used travel distance only and ignored kitchen preparation time
ETA ignores live kitchen preparation times
incidents.fix: Added a fixed 10 minutes to every ETA.
incidents.lesson: A fixed buffer is wrong for every kitchen.

incidents.title: Rider assignment backlog of 4,000 orders at 21:30
incidents.desc: During the semi-final innings break the assignment backlog reached 4,000 orders; average wait for a rider was 22 minutes.
whys: Thousands of orders were waiting for riders
Each assignment batch ran past 60 seconds and the next one queued behind it
Rider assignment runs as one city-wide batch every 60 seconds
incidents.fix: Split Bengaluru into two batches by hand.
incidents.lesson: Every city grows past one batch.

incidents.title: Restaurant tablets missed orders for 15 minutes after a network blip
incidents.desc: After a mobile network blip, tablets in Hyderabad did not show new orders until restaurants restarted them.
whys: Restaurants did not see new orders
Tablets did not reconnect after the connection dropped
The partner tablet keeps one long-poll connection with no reconnect

incidents.title: Refunds for cancelled orders not received after 7 days
incidents.desc: Refunds for 1,300 cancelled orders failed at the gateway and were never retried; customers complained on social media.
whys: Customers did not get refunds
Refund requests that failed at the gateway were never retried or checked
Refunds are never reconciled with the payment gateway
incidents.fix: Re-sent the failed refunds from a report.
incidents.lesson: Nobody looks at failed refunds until people complain.

incidents.title: Order placement failing with 'pool exhausted' at 20:45
incidents.desc: New orders failed for 12 minutes at the start of the second innings while the hourly sales report ran.
whys: New orders failed for 12 minutes
The hourly sales report job held most database connections
Analytics batch jobs share the order database connection pool
incidents.lesson: Reports should never compete with orders.

incidents.title: Match-day coupon not applying for eligible users
incidents.desc: The MATCHDAY coupon failed for eligible users because the code still had last season's dates.
whys: The coupon was rejected for eligible users
The campaign rule was hard-coded with last season's dates
Coupon rules are hard-coded for each campaign

incidents.title: Order tracking errors during the final over
incidents.desc: In the final over of a league match, tracking failed for 10 minutes under polling traffic.
whys: Tracking failed for 10 minutes
Polling traffic from open apps overloaded the tracking API
Apps poll order status every 2 seconds with no backoff

incidents.title: Checkout showed old prices after restaurants updated menus
incidents.desc: Customers saw a higher total at payment than in the cart after restaurants raised prices for the match.
whys: Customers saw a different total at payment
Cart priced items from the stale menu cache
Menu availability is cached without invalidation when restaurants change it
incidents.lesson: The cache is wrong in three places now.

incidents.title: Double charge when the payment page was refreshed
incidents.desc: Refreshing the payment page during a slow UPI response created a second payment for 150 orders.
whys: Customers were charged twice
Refreshing created a second payment for the same order
Payments are created without an idempotency key per order
incidents.lesson: Retries and refreshes both need a key.

incidents.title: Rainy-night ETAs off by 40 minutes
incidents.desc: During heavy rain ETAs stayed at 20 minutes while deliveries took an hour.
whys: ETAs were wrong in the rain
ETA ignored kitchen load and slower rides
ETA ignores live kitchen preparation times
incidents.fix: Added a rain buffer by hand.
incidents.lesson: Buffers do not know which kitchen is busy.

incidents.title: Refunds pending for cancelled IPL-night orders
incidents.desc: Refunds for orders cancelled on match night are still pending; the gateway rejected a batch and nothing retried it.
whys: Refunds are stuck
The gateway rejected a refund batch and nothing retried it
Refunds are never reconciled with the payment gateway

incidents.title: Riders not assigned for 25 minutes during the semi-final
incidents.desc: At the innings break orders are waiting 25 minutes for a rider in Bengaluru and Pune.
whys: Orders are waiting 25 minutes for riders
Assignment batches are overlapping again
Rider assignment runs as one city-wide batch every 60 seconds

incidents.title: Order-delivered notifications sent 30 minutes late
incidents.desc: Customers received 'Your order is on the way' after it had arrived.
whys: Notifications were late
Push notifications are sent inline and were dropped under load
Push notifications are sent synchronously without a queue

debts.title: Assign riders continuously from a per-zone queue of workers
debts.desc: Each zone has its own queue and worker that assigns riders as orders arrive, instead of one city-wide batch every minute.
debts.cause: Rider assignment runs as one city-wide batch every 60 seconds

debts.title: Invalidate the menu cache when a restaurant changes availability or prices
debts.desc: Publish an event on every availability or price change and invalidate the cached menu for that restaurant at once.
debts.cause: Menu availability is cached without invalidation when restaurants change it

debts.title: Reconnect partner tablets with backoff and redeliver missed orders
debts.desc: Tablets reconnect with exponential backoff and jitter after any drop and fetch every order created while they were away.
debts.cause: The partner tablet keeps one long-poll connection with no reconnect

debts.title: Move coupon rules into configuration
debts.desc: Campaign eligibility, dates and limits become configuration that marketing can change without a release.
debts.cause: Coupon rules are hard-coded for each campaign

debts.title: Idempotency key per order for payments
debts.desc: Create at most one payment per order: a second tap or a refresh returns the payment already in progress.
debts.cause: Payments are created without an idempotency key per order

debts.title: Backoff for order-status polling, with pushed updates
debts.desc: Apps poll with backoff from 5 to 30 seconds and receive pushed updates at each milestone, instead of polling every 2 seconds.
debts.cause: Apps poll order status every 2 seconds with no backoff

debts.title: Capture structured kitchen preparation times for ETA
debts.desc: Restaurants report structured preparation times per dish and current kitchen load; ETA uses them along with traffic and rain.
debts.cause: ETA ignores live kitchen preparation times

debts.title: Reconcile refunds with the payment gateway every hour
debts.desc: An hourly job matches every refund with the gateway's report and retries any that failed.
debts.cause: Refunds are never reconciled with the payment gateway

debts.title: Separate connection pools for order writes and analytics batch jobs
debts.desc: Reports and other batch jobs get their own small pool on a read replica so they can never starve order placement.
debts.cause: Analytics batch jobs share the order database connection pool

debts.title: Serve area restaurant lists from a precomputed cache
debts.desc: Precompute the restaurant list for each delivery area every minute and serve it cached, instead of searching on every app open.

debts.title: Send push notifications through a durable queue
debts.desc: Order milestones publish to a durable queue; workers send push and SMS without slowing the order path.
debts.cause: Push notifications are sent synchronously without a queue

debts.title: Index menu items by restaurant and availability
debts.desc: Add a composite index on (restaurant, available) so menu reads do not scan every dish.

debts.title: Load test match-night dispatch at 10x
debts.desc: Replay an IPL innings break at 10 times normal orders against staging before the playoffs.

debts.title: Rate limits and device checks on coupon redemption
debts.desc: Rate limit coupon checks per account, device and IP, and require a verified phone number before a coupon can be redeemed, so bots cannot farm a leaked code.

debts.title: Use IST for coupon validity windows
debts.desc: Coupon start and end times are stored and checked in IST.

spike.description: Dinner orders build from 19:00 and peak at the innings break around 21:15 at nine times a normal busy hour, with a second rush after the match ends.
